To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
functional connectivity within the default mode network was significantly lower in PD compared with HC, and that functional connectivity was significantly greater in PDVh compared with PDnonVh.

1) The default mode network, an intrinsic brain network that is active when an individual is at rest, is abnormal in Parkinson’s disease patients with and without visual hallucinations; and 2) the degree of abnormality of this brain network is greater in Parkinson’s disease with hallucinations than Parkinson’s disease without hallucinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of visual hallucinations in patients with Parkinson’s disease.
the neural basis of visual hallucinations (Vh) in Parkinson's Disease (PD).
the study of the neural basis of the visual hallucination in Parkinson's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the default mode network is altered in Parkinson’s disease with visual hallucination, and the functional coactivation within the default mode network was found to be significantly lower in both the PD with visual hallucination and the PD without visual hallucination groups relative to the healthy control group.
the DMN is disrupted in Parkinson's disease with visual Hallucinations and this disruption is more pronounced in the hallucination positive group compared to the hallucination negative group.
the DMN in PD is functionally abnormal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the default mode network is dysfunctional in patients with Parkinson's disease with visual hallcinations.
the DMN is functionally abnormal in Parkinson’s disease (PD) and the functional connectivity within the network is lower in PD compared to controls.
we have found a network of brain areas that is more active in PD patients with visual hallucinations than in those without hallucinations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have found that the brain network that is most disrupted in Parkinson's disease with visual Hallucinations is the default mode network.

we have shown for the first time, that the brain network which is involved in our normal day to day thoughts and mind wandering is disrupted in Parkinson's disease with visual hallcinations, and this disruption is associated with visual hallucinations in Parkinson's disease.

we have demonstrated for the first time in PD that functional connectivity in the DMN is abnormal, and that this functional abnormality is more pronounced in patients with visual hallucinations compared to those without visual hallucinations.
